name: The Common Thread
summary: A community review told as a newspaper: shared activity receives editorial weight without turning counts into impact claims.

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 9 / big.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 9 / page.

recognitionRules: Set the Georgia masthead above paired horizontal rules, with issue information aligned to its right.
Use narrow narrative columns beside a workbench illustration rather than a grid of corporate statistic cards.
Make large section numbers a reading route; burgundy identifies bylines and editorial emphasis.
Keep participation counts separate from repair or learning outcomes.

principles: Make the invitation warm and the practical details exact.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: A year of small repairs deserves a careful record.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid speaking for an entire community or implying confirmed attendance.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Come for the part that interests you; here is what to expect.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use the full Georgia masthead with a thick-over-thin rule pair. No standalone emblem is necessary.

adaptations: A one-page issue may retain one image, one count and one attributed story.
Use black-only paired rules in economical print editions.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: One half of the capital T height around the masthead, measured outside the paired rules.

minimumSize.status: Conservative production recommendation after inspection at primary220px, secondary180px and symbols32/64px. Trial Ledger record code and Orbit descriptor motivate larger full-lockup minima; use secondary in narrow spaces.
